results.content: arXiv:2505.22803v1 [cs.LG] 28 May 2025 CLUE: Neural Networks Calibration via Learning Uncertainty–Error alignment Pedro Mendes1,2, Paolo Romano2, David Garlan1 1Software and Societal Systems Department, Carnegie Mellon University 2INESC-ID and Instituto Superior Técnico, Universidade de Lisboa Abstract Reliable uncertainty estimation is critical for deploying neural networks (NNs) in real-world applications. In this work, we introduce CLUE (Calibration via Learning Uncertainty–Error Alignment), a novel approach that explicitly aligns predicted uncertainty with observed error during training, grounded in the principle that well-calibrated models should produce uncertainty estimates that match their empirical loss. Through extensive experiments on vision, regression, and language modeling tasks, including out-of-distribution and domain-shift scenarios, we demonstrate that CLUE achieves superior calibration quality and competitive predictive per-formance with respect to state of the art approaches without imposing significant computational overhead. Recent efforts that tackled this problem can be divided into two main categories: (i) post-processing methods, which adjust the model’s predicted probabilities [13, 70, 42, 31, 25, 61, 10] after training using a separate validation set; and (ii) training-time methods, which incorporate calibration objectives directly into the loss function to encourage accurate uncertainty estimation during learning [36, 40, 29, 58, 35, 56, 20]. approaches, while typically more computationally demanding, have shown superior performance in calibration and uncertainty estimation by incorporating uncertainty modeling directly into the learning process [35, 41, 36, 40]. Thus, this work introduces CLUE (Calibration via Learning Uncertainty–Error alignment), a novel training method that improves uncertainty estimation in NNs by ensuring that predicted uncertainty aligns with the model’s error. 2 Background In the current section, we formally define the problem of correctly estimating the uncertainty of NNs and review and discuss existing methods to quantify the uncertainty of NNs. 2.1 Problem Formulation Intuitively, the goal of calibrating neural models is to ensure that the predictive uncertainty of a model aligns with its true probability of correctness. To enhance robustness, CLUE estimates both predictions and uncertainties during training and inference by employing stochastic inference techniques such as MC Dropout, which aggregates outputs from multiple forward passes through the model. Regression Models: In regression benchmarks (see Table 2), CLUE achieves consistently strong performance in both predictive accuracy and uncertainty estimation. 5 Conclusion We introduced CLUE, a general calibration framework for NNs that aligns predictive uncertainty with model error through a scalable and differentiable loss.
